# Plan founder and key-person succession

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When the company becomes dependent on a founder or other person for decisions, relationships or critical access. A tested continuity and succession plan with lawful authority, alternate owners and protected access.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Outcomes

- A tested continuity and succession plan with lawful authority, alternate owners and protected access.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Identify key-person dependencies

agent-runnable


Inventory critical decisions, customer relationships, technical knowledge, signing powers and system ownership concentrated in one person. Record the business impact of their absence without publishing credentials or personal details.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Agree emergency and long-term authority

human · human approval required


The board and counsel establish how replacement decisions, delegations and communications will work. Resolve governing-document restrictions and distinguish temporary cover from permanent appointment or ownership transfer.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare handover and access-recovery instructions

agent-runnable


Write role-specific runbooks, contacts and evidence locations. Use the company access-recovery process and restricted vaults; the succession document should point to authorized access rather than contain raw secrets.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Exercise a realistic absence scenario

human · human approval required


Have designated alternates perform a tabletop handover and authorized access check. Record decisions they could not make, unavailable information and counterparty mandates needing updates.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Close gaps and schedule a review

agent-runnable


Assign remediation owners and verify the corrected runbooks with the alternates. Refresh the plan after financing, leadership or critical-system changes and retain the exercise record.

- Verify: A tested continuity and succession plan with lawful authority, alternate owners and protected access.
- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)
